transcript.content: Hi, welcome. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I don’t really care about anything anymore. Like, I used to go to art classes, and board-game nights—there was this one game with little wooden sheep pieces, I don’t know why I remember that—but now I just don’t go. Hiking, soccer, all of it… I keep thinking I should get back to the team, but then I just sit in my room and everything kind of slips away.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… most days, honestly. I wake up and it’s like this heavy, hollow feeling right here in my chest. Like there’s just… nothing ahead of me, no future past the apartment walls. Which sounds dramatic, I know, but it’s how it feels. Sometimes I stare at the little crack near the window and think I should fix it, but then I don’t, and the whole day just kind of sits there with me.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I think it got… really constant around the next summer. Like before that it came and went a little, or I could distract myself with things, but that summer it just kind of settled in and didn’t leave.

So… about a year and four months now, I guess. It’s weird because I remember the heat more than the actual days—my apartment gets so stuffy, and I kept meaning to buy a fan, but I didn’t. Since then it’s just been there most of the time.
Before this started about a year and four months ago, was there ever another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for weeks at a time?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had bad stretches before, I think… like in school I remember missing classes for a while, but I also missed them because the parking situation was impossible and the one professor always started early, which drove me crazy.

But weeks like this? I don’t know. It’s hard to separate out. My memory kind of turns into piles, like “that was a bad year” or “that apartment had weird carpet,” not exact periods. I wouldn’t want to say yes if I’m not sure.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead?

Yeah… I mean, I keep having these thoughts where I just don’t want to wake up anymore. Not exactly like I’m making some… plan in that moment, but more like if I could just not have to open my eyes and do another day, that would be better.

And—this is embarrassing—I guess my friend found me once when I was really not okay, and I was saying out loud that I couldn’t keep living like this. I don’t even remember everything I said, I just remember the look on her face, and then I got distracted thinking I should’ve cleaned the kitchen before she came over, which is stupid, but… yeah. That’s been happening.
Did this start after a major stressful event or change in your life?

Yeah… I think it was after the divorce. Not right that second, because there were all these practical things, papers and moving stuff around, and I remember arguing with the cable company for like an hour because they kept transferring me to the wrong department.

But shortly after that, it really started. So… I guess it’s been about a year and eleven months now. Almost two years, which feels strange to say out loud.
During these past two years, have there been any stretches as long as two months when you were not feeling depressed?

No… I don’t think so. Not two months. I mean, there are little pieces where I can seem okay, like I’ll watch half a show or I’ll go to the store and think the oranges look really bright, and then I come home and it’s just… back.

Most of the time since this all took over, I haven’t just been scared or mixed up or whatever. I’ve been really, really depressed. Like barely interested in anything, and this feeling like my life is already over even though I’m still walking around in it. So no, I can’t think of a stretch that long where it actually lifted.
When you’re at your lowest, have you heard voices that other people couldn’t hear?

Yeah… yes. It’s usually this woman’s voice, from the corner of my room. I know that sounds like a weird detail, the corner—there’s this little pile of laundry there sometimes, and I keep meaning to move it, and then I don’t, and—

But the voice is clear. Like someone is standing right next to my bed, not like a thought in my head. She says I ruined everything and that I should just stay inside. It gets… really hard to tell myself it isn’t real when it sounds that close.
Before this current depression began, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed like this nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I’m… not sure. I mean, I had sad times before, like breakups or when school got overwhelming, but I don’t know if it was like this nearly every day for two weeks.

It’s hard to separate it out now, because this last couple years kind of colors everything when I look back. Like I remember being down in college, but I also remember missing class because I couldn’t find parking and then just sitting in my car, and that might’ve been stress, not the same thing. So… I don’t really know.
Before this depression began, was there ever a time when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I don’t really know. I keep trying to line it up in my head, like before all this started… but it gets messy.

There were times I was sad, I think, or kind of shut down, but I can’t say for sure it was nearly every day for two weeks. I remember this one semester where I kept buying notebooks because I thought if I had a fresh one I’d get organized, and then I’d just leave them in the car. But I don’t know if that was depression or just me not handling things well.

So… I’m not sure. I can’t give you a clean yes or no.
Before this current depression started, was there ever a time when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I mean, before this one, I’m still not totally sure how to separate it out. But right now, most days I wake up and there’s this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest, like… like there isn’t any future for me past the apartment walls.

And I know you asked before it started—sorry, I’m trying to answer that. It’s just when I think back, everything gets kind of blurred together, like the apartment, the mornings, the same dishes in the sink, and I can’t tell where one bad stretch ended and another started.
Before this depression began, was there ever a time in your life when you were depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks and then got better before this current episode started?

I… I don’t know if there was a clear time like that. Like, a time where it was nearly every day for two weeks and then I got better before this one started… I can’t really pin that down.

I keep thinking of bits and pieces, like being in bed too long, or getting behind on stuff, but then I remember other random things from the same time, like driving around for no reason or rearranging my closet, and it all kind of mixes together. I don’t have a clean “yes, that happened and then it ended.” I’m sorry.
Before this depression began, was there ever a time when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks and then returned to your usual self before it started?

I’m trying to think about the “returned to my usual self” part, and I don’t really know. Right now it’s like… most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest, like there’s no future for me beyond the apartment walls.

Before this started, I can remember bad stretches, but I can’t tell if I ever fully came back to normal in between. It’s hard to separate it cleanly.
Before this depression started, do you remember ever having a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day and then later returned to your usual self?

I’m not sure I can say that, no. I keep trying to line it up in my head like a calendar, like “this was two weeks and then I was normal,” but it doesn’t really come back that neatly.

There were definitely times I felt low, but whether it was nearly every day and then I actually got back to my usual self… I don’t know. It all kind of blends together. Like I’ll remember one bad stretch, and then suddenly I’m thinking about where I was living then, or what the weather was like, or some random argument I had, and I lose the thread. So I don’t want to say yes if I can’t really remember it clearly.
Before this current depression, was there ever a time when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks and then later returned to your usual self?

I don’t think I can answer that clearly. I keep trying to look back and see if there was a neat chunk of time where I was depressed every day and then I was “back to myself,” but it doesn’t feel neat like that.

It’s more like… I remember little pieces, like certain rooms I was in, or a song I kept playing, or feeling like I was dragging myself around, and then I get sidetracked thinking about what else was happening then. So I can’t honestly say yes, there was a definite two-week thing and then I got better. I just don’t know.
Before this current depression started, do you remember ever having a separate period when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I’m sorry, I know you’re asking something specific, but I still can’t really pin that down. I remember being depressed before, or at least feeling really low, but I don’t know if it was most of the day almost every day for two full weeks as its own separate thing.

When I try to think back, I start remembering odd details instead, like where I was sitting or what the light looked like in the room, and then I lose the actual timeline. So… I can’t honestly say yes. I just don’t remember it clearly enough.
Before this current depression, do you remember a time when you had depression that lasted at least two weeks and then completely went away before this episode began?

I don’t really remember it that cleanly. Like, I can think of times I was really down, but whether it lasted two weeks and then completely went away before this… I don’t know.

It’s hard because when I try to look back, I start thinking about other things from that time, like what apartment I was in or what I was doing during the day, and then I lose track of the actual feeling part. So I can’t honestly say there was a clear episode that ended and I was totally fine after. I’m just not sure.
Before this depression began, do you remember ever having a separate period of depression that fully ended?

I don’t really know. I’m trying to answer it the right way, but “fully ended” is where I get stuck. Like, I can remember being low before, but I can’t tell if it was a separate period that stopped completely, or if I just got distracted by life for a while.

Sometimes I remember things around it more than the depression itself, like what I was wearing or some random errand I had to do, and then I lose the thread. So… I can’t really say yes, there was a clear depression that fully ended before this one.
Before this current depression, did you ever have a separate depressive episode that later ended?

I’m still not sure. I know I’ve had times before this where I felt really low, but I can’t separate it out clearly enough to say, “that was an episode, and then it ended.”

It’s like when I try to remember, I get pulled into all these little details that don’t help—like what the room looked like, or what bus route I was taking then—and then I lose the actual answer. So I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure. I just can’t tell if there was a separate depressive episode that later ended.
Before this depression started, do you remember ever having another separate period of depression that got better before this one began?

I don’t think I can pin that down. I mean, there were times before where I remember feeling bad, but then I start thinking about everything around that time, like where I was living or what I was doing during the day, and it gets kind of mixed up.

So if you mean a clear separate depression that got better before this one started, I’m not sure. I don’t want to say yes and then be wrong.
